en: The Scripture of the Names of Buddhas Spoken by the Buddha, Volume One.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci at the residence of the Duke of Qin, Tai Shang Wenxuan Gong, Marquis of Hu.
At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park, together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus.
At that time, the World-Honored One was surrounded by the fourfold assembly, as well as devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the great assembly:
I shall speak for you of the names of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present."

If good sons or good daughters receive, uphold, read, and recite the names of the Buddhas, these people will enjoy peace and security in the present life, remain far removed from all calamities, and extinguish all their transgressions; furthermore, they shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in the future.
If a son or daughter of good family wishes to eliminate all transgressions, they should bathe and purify themselves, put on new, clean clothes, kneel with palms joined, and speak these words:

“Homage to Akṣobhya Buddha of the East; homage to Arciṣmat Buddha; homage to Vimalanetra Buddha; homage to Abhaya Buddha; homage to Acintya Buddha; homage to Dīparāja Buddha; homage to Raśmipramukta Buddha; homage to Prabhāvyūha Buddha; homage to Mahāvijaya Buddha; homage to Mahārthasiddhi Buddha; homage to Tattvadarśin Buddha; homage to Dṛḍharājapuṣpa Buddha. I take refuge in the Buddhas of the East, such as these, who are immeasurable and boundless.”

“Namo to the Buddha Samantapūrṇa of the southern quarter; namo to the Buddha Vīrarāja; namo to the Buddha Dhṛtiparākrama; namo to the Buddha Prajñājñāna; namo to the Buddha Yaśasvara; namo to the Buddha Anikṣiptadarśanavigraha; namo to the Buddha Siṃhasvara; namo to the Buddha Amoghadarśin; namo to the Buddha Cāritramati; namo to the Buddha Sarvacaryāviśuddha; namo to the Buddha Vyūharāja; namo to the Buddha Mahāparvatarāja. I take refuge in the Buddhas of the southern quarter, such as these, who are immeasurable and boundless.”

“Namo to the Buddha Amitāyus of the western quarter; namo to the Buddha Siṃha; namo to the Buddha Gandhottamakūṭa; namo to the Buddha Gandhapāṇi; namo to the Buddha Vikrāntagāmin; namo to the Buddha Gaganagañja; namo to the Buddha Ratnaketu; namo to the Buddha Viśuddhanetra; namo to the Buddha Priyadarśana; namo to the Buddha Ratnagiri; namo to the Buddha Prabhārāja; namo to the Buddha Candrodayaprabha. I take refuge in the Buddhas of the western quarter, such as these, who are immeasurable and boundless.”

“Namo to the Buddha Difficult to Conquer of the North; namo to the Buddha Moonlight; namo to the Buddha Sandalwood; namo to the Buddha Sovereign; namo to the Buddha Golden-Colored King; namo to the Buddha Sandalwood Moonlight; namo to the Buddha Universal Eye-Seeing; namo to the Buddha Universal Illumination Eye-Seeing; namo to the Buddha Wheel-Hand; namo to the Buddha Stainless. We take refuge in the Buddhas of the North, such as these, who are immeasurable and boundless.”

"Homage to the Buddha Bhūmipariśodhana of the southeast; homage to the Buddha Īśvara; homage to the Buddha Dharmeśvara; homage to the Buddha Dharmamati; homage to the Buddha Dharmacintin; homage to the Buddha Nityadharmamati; homage to the Buddha Nityasukha; homage to the Buddha Sucintita; homage to the Buddha Susthita; homage to the Buddha Subāhu. We take refuge in these and all other immeasurable and boundless Buddhas of the southeastern direction."

“Namo to the Buddha Nārāyaṇa in the southwest; namo to the Buddha Dragon-King Virtue; namo to the Buddha Jewel Sound; namo to the Buddha Earth Sovereign; namo to the Buddha Human King; namo to the Buddha Wondrous Sound; namo to the Buddha Wisdom; namo to the Buddha Wondrous Fragrant Flower; namo to the Buddha Heavenly King; namo to the Buddha Constantly Pure Eye. I take refuge in these and all other immeasurable and boundless Buddhas of the southwest.”

“Namo to the Buddha Moonlight Face of the Northwest; Namo to the Buddha Moonlight; Namo to the Buddha Moon Banner; Namo to the Buddha Valiant; Namo to the Buddha Sunlight Face; Namo to the Buddha Sun Treasury; Namo to the Buddha Adorned with Sunlight; Namo to the Buddha Flower Body; Namo to the Buddha Padma Treasury; Namo to the Buddha Padma Beard; Namo to the Buddha Lion’s Roar King; Namo to the Buddha Well-Abiding Mind. We take refuge in these and all other immeasurable, boundless Buddhas of the northwest.”

“Homage to the Buddha Śāntendriya in the northeast; homage to the Buddha Śānti; homage to the Buddha Mahāsena; homage to the Buddha Viśuddhajaya; homage to the Buddha Viśuddhasusvara; homage to the Buddha Viśuddhadevapūjita; homage to the Buddha Sukhavivarta; homage to the Buddha Vivarta; homage to the Buddha Sumati; homage to the Buddha Sumatidhara. We take refuge in all such infinite and boundless Buddhas of the northeast.”

“Namo to the Buddha of True Practice in the lower direction; Namo to the Buddha Swift Gait; Namo to the Buddha Wise Wisdom; Namo to the Buddha Firm King; Namo to the Buddha Vajra-Like Peak; Namo to the Buddha Lion; Namo to the Buddha Vigorous Stride; Namo to the Buddha Abiding in Reality; Namo to the Buddha Accomplished Merit; Namo to the Buddha Attained Merit; Namo to the Buddha Well-Established in Bliss; Namo to the Buddha Celestial Vajra. I take refuge in these and all other immeasurable and boundless Buddhas of the lower direction.”

“Namo to the Buddha Immeasurable Victory above; Namo to the Buddha Cloud King; Namo to the Buddha Cloud Virtue; Namo to the Buddha Immeasurable Renown; Namo to the Buddha King of Renowned Body; Namo to the Buddha Great Virtue; Namo to the Buddha Great Sumeru; Namo to the Buddha Subduer of Māra. I take refuge in these and all other immeasurable, boundless Buddhas of the zenith.”

“Namo to the future Samantabhadra Buddha; namo to Maitreya Buddha; namo to Avalokiteśvara Buddha; namo to Mahāsthāmaprāpta Buddha; namo to Gaganagañja Buddha; namo to Vimalakīrti Buddha; namo to Arthasiddha Buddha; namo to Satyaghoṣa Buddha; namo to Mahāsāgara Buddha; namo to Akṣayamati Buddha. I take refuge in these and all other such infinite and boundless Buddhas of the future.”

“Good sons and good daughters, by upholding, receiving, reading, and reciting the names of these Buddhas, you shall enjoy peace and security in the present life, remain far removed from all calamities, and have all your transgressions extinguished; furthermore, in the future, you will ultimately attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”

“Homage to the Buddha Vimalaprabha; homage to the Buddha Ruciravyūhacintin; homage to the Buddha Vimalacandradhvajaśrī; homage to the Buddha Puṣpārāma; homage to the Buddha Tejorāśi; homage to the Buddha Ratnottama; homage to the Buddha Abhayadṛśa; homage to the Buddha Sarvabhayatrāsāpagata; homage to the Buddha Siṃhavikrāntabalasamudgata; homage to the Buddha Suvarṇaprabhāsavirāja. If a son of good family or a daughter of good family recites and contemplates these names of the Buddhas for ten days, they will certainly be freed from all karmic obstructions.

At that time, the bhikṣus addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One! World-Honored One!
Are the lifespans of all these Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, equal in length?”
"Listen attentively, and I shall speak for you.
One kalpa in this Sahā world, the land of Śākyamuni Buddha of the Bhadrakalpa, constitutes one day and night in the Land of Peace and Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
One kalpa in the Land of Peace and Bliss, the realm of Amitābha Buddha, constitutes one day and night in the world of Kāṣāyadhvaja.

One eon in the world-system of Saṃghāṭadhvaja, the buddha-field of Vajrapramardana, is a single day and night in the world-system of Avaivartacakranirghoṣa, the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Padmavikrāntagāmin Suprabha.
One eon in the world-system *Avivartyacakra-nirghoṣa* is a single day and night in the land of the Tathāgata *Dharmadhvaja* in the world-system *Vimalā*.
One eon in the world-system *Vimalā* is a single day and night in the land of the Tathāgata *Siṃha* in the world-system *Supratapita*.
One kalpa in the world Sukhapradīpa is one day and night in the land of the Tathāgata Vairocanagarbha in the world Suprabhā.
One kalpa in the world Suprabhā is one day and night in the land of the Tathāgata Dharmaprabhāpadmavyūhakāya in the world Duratikrama.
If one kalpa in the world Difficult-to-Cross were a single day and night in the land of the Tathāgata Sarvābhijñāprabha in the world Adorned Wisdom;
and if one kalpa in the world Adorned Wisdom were a single day and night in the land of the Tathāgata Candramatī in the world Mirror-Wheel Radiance.

"Monks! Entering into such a calculation, it takes as long as ten hundred thousand koṭis of asaṃkhyeya worlds to reach the final world, Padmottara; in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Bhadraśrī, that constitutes one day and one night."

In this manner, these worlds are immeasurable and boundless, differing in length and duration; likewise, the lifespans and periods of abiding in the world of the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, are also such."
“O Bhikṣus! You should all invoke the names of these Buddhas, speaking thus:
‘Homage to these Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and so forth.’”

Namo to the Buddha Sarvavyūha. At that time, the bhikṣu Upamāna rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
How many Buddhas have passed away?
The Buddha told the bhikṣu Upamaṇa:

“Bhikṣus! Suppose there were worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, from the bottom reaching down to the water’s edge, up to the very summit of existence (bhavāgra), filled with fine motes of dust.

Suppose there were someone who took that many atoms from within it, and after crossing worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, dropped one atom; and after crossing further worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, dropped another atom; in this manner, they exhausted all those atoms.
Whether those atoms are placed together or not placed together, would it be possible to know the number of those atoms?"
“Monks! Those motes of dust may have their number known, but those past Buddhas named Śākyamuni who have already entered parinirvāṇa cannot be numbered.”
I know those past Buddhas as if seeing them before my eyes.

The mothers of those Buddhas were all named Mahāmāyā; their fathers were all named King Śuddhodana; their cities were all named Kapilavastu; and their foremost śrāvaka disciples were all named Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana, and their attendant disciples were all named Ānanda—let alone their various other names for mothers, fathers, cities, disciples, and attendants."

"Monks! Regarding those various worlds, in which of them that person places a mote of dust and in which he does not—whether those worlds where a mote of dust is placed or where it is not—extending from the lower limit of the water's edge up to the peak of existence."

"Monks! Furthermore, suppose there were a second person who takes up a single mote of dust and, having passed as many worlds as the number of those motes of dust—that is, as many Buddha-fields as there are *asaṃkhyeya* hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *nayuta*s of worlds—takes this as one step."

"Monks! That person takes as many worlds as there are atoms in those [previously mentioned] numbers as a single step. Walking in this manner for hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of asamkhyeya kalpas, he places down a single atom; in this way, he exhausts all the atoms."
"Monks! Suppose there were as many worlds as there are motes of dust filling all those worlds, and one were to further place them within the worlds of the ten directions. Monks!"
Furthermore, beyond these worlds, one places atoms; in those worlds, from the water's edge below up to the peak of existence above, they are filled with atoms.
"What do you think? Can the number of those atoms be known?

“The number of those atoms may be known, but the number of those who share the same name as mother, the same name as father, the same name as city, the same name as disciple, the same name as attendant, and the same name as Śākyamuni Buddha—these cannot be known.”
As it is with Śākyamuni Buddha, so it is with Anabhibhūdhvaja Buddha; as it is with Rocana Buddha, so it is with Vimalajayacakṣus Buddha.
Vimala-prabhā-netra Buddha was also like this.
Su-vimala-viśuddha Buddha was also like this."
“Sugata Anantaguṇasamudgatarāja Buddha was likewise. Ratnaprabhāsa Buddha was likewise.
Śāntabhū Buddha was likewise. Yaśaḥkīrti Buddha was likewise. Padmottara Buddha was likewise. Candrasūrya Buddha was likewise. Samantaratnacchatra Buddha was likewise.”
“Monks! You should take refuge in these and other such incalculable Buddhas who share the same name.
‘Homage to the Buddha Universal Radiance Exertion King (Samantaprabha-vikrama-rāja).’”

"Homage to the Buddha Bhadra-viśeṣa-jaya in the world-system Aśoka. "If any son or daughter of good family upholds the name of this Buddha, they will certainly attain non-retrogression from bodhi."
“Homage to the Buddha Candana-viśeṣa in the world Nanda. If any good man or good woman upholds the name of this Buddha, they will ultimately attain a pure mind.”

“Namo to the Buddha Śāntarañjana of the world Bhadra; namo to the Buddha Mārabalaprakampana of the world Manojña-ke-tu; namo to the Buddha Aśoka of the world Pūrṇacandra; namo to the Buddha Ratnadaṇḍa of the world Ke-tu-manas-vijaya; namo to the Buddha Puṣpavijaya of the world Vāgghoṣavijaya; namo to the Buddha Traivikrama of the world Kṣema; namo to the Buddha Drumarājavijaya of the world Vipula; namo to the Buddha Vajraguṇakāya of the world Candravijaya; and namo to the Buddha Sāgaravijaya of the past, immeasurable and boundless. “If a son of good family recites the names of those Buddhas, he shall attain the bodhicitta that is ultimately non-retrogressive.”

"Namo to the Buddha Meruśikhararāja! When that Buddha first attained enlightenment, his first assembly consisted of eighty billion *koṭi-nayuta* śrāvakas; his second assembly, seventy billion *koṭi-nayuta*; his third assembly, sixty billion *koṭi-nayuta*; and his fourth assembly, twenty-five billion *koṭi-nayuta*. Likewise, there were immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *nayuta* bodhisattvas."

“Homage to the Buddha Siṃhaghoṣarāja! That Tathāgata’s first assembly consisted of nine hundred and ninety million śrāvakas; the second assembly, nine billion; the third assembly, nine hundred and thirty million; and the fourth assembly, nine hundred and ninety million. Likewise, the multitude of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas was immeasurable and boundless.”
“Homage to the Buddha Puṣpavijaya. In that Buddha’s first assembly, there were eight billion śrāvakas, and the community of bodhisattvas was likewise.
“Homage to the Buddha Sucarita. In that Buddha’s first assembly, there were eight billion śrāvakas, and the community of bodhisattvas was likewise.

“Homage to the Buddha of Immeasurable Great Adornments. In that Buddha’s first assembly, there were eight billion śrāvakas; in the second assembly, seven billion; and so on, up to the tenth assembly, which was likewise. The assembly of bodhisattvas was also thus immeasurable and boundless.

“Homage to the Buddha Radiant Flame! Homage to the Buddha Majestic Virtue! In that Buddha’s first assembly, there were nine hundred billion śrāvakas; likewise for the second through the tenth assemblies. The saṃgha of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas was immeasurable and boundless.
“Homage to the Buddha Sarvālokakara! In that Buddha’s first assembly, there were *nayuta* of billions of śrāvakas, and the community of bodhisattvas was likewise.”

“Homage to the Buddha Immeasurable Radiance! In that Buddha’s first assembly, there were nine hundred and sixty million śrāvakas; in the second assembly, nine hundred and forty million; and in the third assembly, nine hundred and twenty million. The assembly of bodhisattvas was likewise.”

“Homage to the Buddha Śabdaguṇa. In that Buddha’s first assembly, there were eight billion śrāvakas; in the second assembly, seven billion; and in the third assembly, six billion. The assembly of bodhisattvas was likewise.
"One should take refuge in these and other such infinite and boundless Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

One should pay homage to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the Pure and Stainless World in the southern direction, namely Mañjuśrī, who currently resides within the Buddha-land of the Tathāgata Samantadarśin."
Furthermore, monks! You should pay homage to the four great bodhisattvas:

the first is named Prabhāketu, who currently resides in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Abhaya in the east; the second is named Jñānavijaya, who currently resides in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Jñānaskandha in the south; the third is named Śāntendriya, who currently resides in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Jñānaparvata in the west; and the fourth is named Manorathasiddhi, who currently resides in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Nārāyaṇa in the north.
"Homage to the Bodhisattva Prabhāketu in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Abhayada in the east.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Jñānavijaya in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Jñānaskandha in the south."
"Homage to the Bodhisattva Śāntendriya in the Buddha-field of the Tathāgata Jñānagiri in the western direction.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Manasikārārthasiddhi in the Buddha-field of the Tathāgata Nārāyaṇa in the northern direction."
"Furthermore, the bhikṣu Mahānāman again questioned the Tathāgata:
How many Buddhas of the past have entered parinirvāṇa?'"
“Listen attentively now, and I shall speak for you, bhikṣu.”

In worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the east, worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the south, worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the west, worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the north, and worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the four intermediate directions and above and below—all those worlds, from the bottom to the water’s edge and reaching up to the peak of existence (bhavāgra), were filled with motes of dust.
What do you think? Can the number of those atoms be known?
“In this way, the number of Tathāgatas named Śākyamuni Buddha who have entered parinirvāṇa in the past is beyond calculation.
Monks! I know those past Buddhas as if they were standing before me.”

Those mothers of the Buddhas were all named Mahāmāyā; their fathers were all named King Śuddhodana; their cities were all named Kapilavastu; those Buddhas’ foremost śrāvaka disciples were all named Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana; and their attendant disciples were all named Ānanda—let alone the various different names for mothers, fathers, cities, disciples, and attendants.

"Monks! Regarding those various worlds, whichever worlds that person places particles of dust upon and whichever worlds he does not place particles of dust upon—all those worlds, both those with particles placed upon them and those without—extending downward to the water's edge and upward to the Peak of Existence."

"Monks! Furthermore, there is a second person who takes those atoms; for as many worlds as there are in that number of atoms—namely, as many Buddha-fields, incalculable billions, hundreds of thousands, tens of millions, and nayutas of worlds—he takes a single step past that many worlds."

"Monks! That person takes a single step across as many worlds as there are atoms; in this manner, that person travels for hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of asamkhyeya kalpas before setting down a single atom, until all the atoms have been exhausted."

"Monks! Suppose there were as many worlds as these, whether they were covered with atoms of dust or not; suppose they were filled completely with such atoms, and furthermore, that these atoms were then placed throughout the worlds of the ten directions."

"Monks! Furthermore, beyond these worlds, whether they are occupied by atoms of dust or not, all those worlds—from the bottom reaching down to the water's edge up to the peak of existence—are filled with atoms of dust."
“Bhikṣus! What do you think? Can the number of those atoms be known?

"The number of those atoms may be known; however, the Buddhas named Śākyamuni, their mothers named Mahāmāyā, their fathers named King Śuddhodana, their cities named Kapilavastu, their foremost disciples named Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana, and their attendant disciples named Ānanda, are beyond calculation."

Suppose there is a third person who takes that many world-dust atoms, and for every such number of world-dust atoms passed, he takes one step; traveling for several hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of asaṃkhyeya kalpas, he then sets down a single dust atom, continuing in this manner until all the dust atoms are exhausted.

Furthermore, there is a fourth person who takes as many worlds as there are atoms in those [previously mentioned] worlds—whether they have been set down or not—and fills them with atoms from the bottom, reaching the water's edge, up to the top, reaching the Peak of Existence.
"Monks! What do you think? Can the number of those atoms be known?
"The number of those various atoms may be known;

however, the number of those Buddhas who share the same name as Śākyamuni—sharing the same name for their mothers, the same name for their fathers, the same name for their worlds, the same name for their disciples, the same name for their attendants, and the same name as Buddha—is impossible to know."
"Monks! In this way, there is a fifth person, a sixth, a seventh, an eighth, a ninth, and a tenth person.

Furthermore, there is an eleventh person who takes one atom from among those many atoms and breaks it into as many parts as there are atoms in worlds throughout the ten directions; just as that one atom is broken into as many parts, so too are all the remaining atoms each broken into as many parts as there are atoms in worlds throughout the ten directions.
What do you think? Can the number of those atoms be known?

"Furthermore, suppose there is a person who takes a single step across as many Buddha-lands as there are atoms [in those lands], traveling through the worlds of the eastern direction with such swift supernatural power for immeasurable and boundless eons. Traveling thus through the worlds of the eastern direction, they drop a single atom until the eastern direction is exhausted. Whether those atoms were dropped or not, from the bottom of the water’s edge up to the peak of existence (bhavāgra), it is filled with atoms;
likewise for the southern direction and so on, up to the ten directions, from the bottom of the water’s edge up to the peak of existence, it is filled with atoms."
What do you think? Can the number of those atoms be known?
"The number of atoms [in those lands] may be known;

however, the number of Śākyamuni Buddhas currently existing in the world who have entered nirvana—sharing the same name as the mother Mahāmāyā, the same name as the father Śuddhodana, the same name as the city Kapilavastu, the same names for the disciples Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana, and the same name for the attendant disciple Ānanda—is impossible to know by calculation, let alone those with various different names."
Even if I were to remain in the world for as many eons as there are atoms in a great many worlds, speaking of Buddhas who share the same name Śākyamuni, I could not reach the end of them.

Likewise, there are those with the same name Dīpaṃkara, the same name Tīṣya, the same name Pradīpaprabha, the same name Sarvābhibhū, the same name Yaśas, the same name Padmottara, the same name Vipaśyin, the same name Śikhin, the same name Viśvabhū, the same name Krakucchanda, the same name Kanakamuni, and the same name Kāśyapa. For all such Buddhas with various names—up to their various names for mothers and even their various names for attendants entering parinirvāṇa—I know those Buddhas as if they were standing before me."
"One should pay homage to all such Buddhas as these: 'Homage to the Buddha Śākyamuni of the same name;

homage to the Buddha Dīpaṃkara of the same name; homage to the Buddha Tīṣya of the same name; homage to the Buddha Pradīparāja of the same name; homage to the Buddha Sarvābhibhū of the same name; homage to the Buddha Yaśodhvaja of the same name; homage to the Buddha Padmottara of the same name; homage to the Buddha Vipaśyin of the same name; homage to the Buddha Śikhin of the same name; homage to the Buddha Viśvabhū of the same name; homage to the Buddha Krakucchanda of the same name; homage to the Buddha Kanakamuni of the same name; homage to the Buddha Kāśyapa of the same name. The bhikṣu Upamāna addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One!"
How many Buddhas will there be in the future?
The Buddha told the bhikṣu Upamāna:
“Listen attentively now, and I shall speak for you. Bhikṣus!
In the future, during the Constellation Kalpa (Tārakā-kalpa), three hundred Buddhas will appear in the world, all bearing the same name: Mahākīrti Buddha.”
Furthermore, there were ten thousand Buddhas, all named King Adorned (*Vyūharāja*).

During the eon known as Flower-Made (*Puṣpakṛta*), one billion hundred thousand million Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name: Buddha Awakened by the Flower of Enlightenment (*Bodhivibuddhapuṣpa*).
In the eighth *bimbara* kalpa, Buddhas appeared in the world all sharing the same name, Vītarāga.
During the *tāḷapuṣpa* kalpa, six thousand Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name, Puṣpavarṣa.
"In the eon of Supreme Sound, within the world-system Saravara-īśvara-ucchaya-dhvaja, ten thousand Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name: Pure Utpala Fragrant Mountain Buddha."
"In the Samantakusuma kalpa, one thousand eight hundred Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name, Vītarāga Buddha.
Furthermore, one thousand three hundred Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name, Brahmaghoṣa Buddha."
"Furthermore, in another kalpa, thirty billion Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name, Śākyamuni Buddha.
Again, in another kalpa, eight thousand Buddhas with the same name, Dīpaṃkara Buddha, appeared in the world."
"Furthermore, in another eon, sixty thousand Buddhas named Saṃtuṣita appeared in the world.
Again, in another eon, three hundred million Buddhas appeared in the world, all named Puṣya."
Furthermore, in another kalpa, eighteen thousand buddhas appeared in the world, all bearing the same name Śālendrarāja Buddha—eighty thousand according to the Dan edition.
“Furthermore, there was an eon in which three hundred Buddhas appeared in the world, all named Padmottama Buddha.
Furthermore, there was an eon in which five hundred Buddhas appeared in the world, all named Pāṭhava Buddha.”
"Furthermore, there was an eon in which a thousand Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name, Jambūnada Buddha.
Furthermore, there was an eon in which twelve hundred and eighty million Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name, Sarvārthadarśin Buddha."
"Furthermore, there was an eon in which one thousand Buddhas appeared in the world, all bearing the same name, Krakucchanda Buddha.
Furthermore, there was an eon in which nine thousand Buddhas appeared in the world, all bearing the same name, Kāśyapa Buddha."
"Furthermore, in another kalpa, eighteen Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name, Indra-dhvaja Buddha.
Furthermore, in another kalpa, fifteen Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name, Sūrya Buddha."
"Furthermore, in another kalpa, sixty billion Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name, Mahāvyūha Buddha.
Again, in another kalpa, sixty Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name, Indradhvaja Buddha."
"Furthermore, in another kalpa, five hundred Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name, Sūrya Buddha.
Furthermore, in another kalpa, sixty billion Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name, Mahāvyūha Buddha."
"Furthermore, in another kalpa, six thousand two hundred Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name, Śānticārin Buddha.
Furthermore, in another kalpa, sixty billion Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name, Śālarājendra Buddha."
"Furthermore, in another kalpa, eight thousand buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name, Resolute Diligence Buddha (Dṛḍhavīrya).
Furthermore, in another kalpa, ten billion buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name, Resolute Radiance Buddha (Viniścita-prabhāsa)."
"Furthermore, in another kalpa, eighty billion Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name: Real Dharma Determination Buddha (Saddharmaviniścaya-buddha).
Furthermore, in another kalpa, sixty-two billion Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name: Vairocana Buddha."
“Furthermore, in another kalpa, sixty thousand buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name, Wondrous Padma Buddha (*Miyao Poutuomuo*).
Furthermore, in another kalpa, forty thousand buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name, Adorned by Vows Buddha (*Yuanshuangyan*)."
"Furthermore, in another kalpa, five hundred Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name, Padmavijitendra Buddha.
Furthermore, in another kalpa, forty billion nayutas of Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name, Susvara Buddha."
"Furthermore, there was an eon in which one thousand Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name: Buddha Guṇakūṭaśāntivikrāntagāmin.
Furthermore, there was an eon in which sixty thousand Buddhas appeared in the world, all sharing the same name: Buddha Dṛḍhapraśāntamṛdu."

Furthermore, in another eon, there appeared ten times the number of Buddhas as atoms in a hundred thousand myriads of unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-lands, all sharing the same name, Samantabhadra Buddha.
“Furthermore, in another kalpa, seven thousand Buddhas will appear in the world, all sharing the same name, Dharmavyūharāja Buddha. Bhikṣu!
To speak in brief, the future Buddhas are immeasurable and boundless, unspeakably unspeakable, and inexhaustible.”
You should single-mindedly take refuge in all such Buddhas as these.
At that time, Śāriputra rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
How many Buddhas are currently present?
"I now truly see the Buddha's body.

"I now see throughout the immeasurable, boundless, unspeakably unspeakable worlds of the ten directions those who, like me, are named Śākyamuni Buddha and dwell in the world; they are no different from how you see me."
In this way, there were Buddhas named Dīpaṃkara, Buddhas named Vipaśyin, Buddhas named Śikhin, Buddhas named Viśvabhū, Buddhas named Krakucchanda, Buddhas named Kanakamuni, and Buddhas named Kāśyapa.

“Śāriputra! To speak briefly, even if I were to speak for one eon, or for hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, millions, billions, nayutas of eons, the Buddhas who share the same name could not be fully exhausted; how much more so those with different names?”
All these Buddhas, such as these, were first taught by Mañjuśrī to resolve their minds toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. Śāriputra!
"You should single-mindedly take refuge in all such Buddhas as these.
Śāriputra! In the present eon, there are five hundred Buddhas, all named Jñānaketu."
Furthermore, there was an eon with five hundred Buddhas all named Dharmadhvaja;
another eon with sixty-two Buddhas all named Dīpaṃkara;
and another eon with sixty-two Buddhas all named Śikhin.
Furthermore, there was an eon of one thousand Buddhas, all named Jvalanāgnidāna-īśvara-rāja-ghoṣa Buddha.

There was also an eon of two thousand Buddhas with different names: some were named Jñānavijaya Buddha, some were named Ulkāpradīpa-rāja Buddha, some were named Dharmavijaya Buddha, and some were named Brahmavijaya Buddha.
Śāriputra! You should single-mindedly take refuge in all such Buddhas as these. Śāriputra!
Furthermore, there is a Buddha named Suśvaravibhaktaghoṣa. Śāriputra,
the lifespan of that Buddha Suśvaravibhaktaghoṣa is sixty hundred years.
Passing beyond this to the east, there is the Tathāgata named Jñāneśvara, the Honored One Among Two-Legged Beings; the lifespan of that Tathāgata Jñāneśvara is twelve thousand years.

Passing beyond the World-Honored One Jñāneśvara, there is another Buddha named Ojaseśvara, the Honored One Among Two-Legged Beings; the lifespan of the Buddha Ojaseśvara is seventy-six thousand years.
Passing beyond the World-Honored One of Majestic Virtue and Sovereignty, there is another Buddha named Maheśvara; the lifespan of that Buddha Maheśvara is a full one hundred million years.
Beyond the Buddha Mahesvara, there was another Buddha named Brahmaghoṣa; the lifespan of that Buddha Brahmaghoṣa was a full ten billion years.
Beyond the World-Honored One Brahmaghoṣa, there was another Buddha named Mahāgaṇeśvara; the lifespan of that Buddha Mahāgaṇeśvara was a full sixty thousand years.
Passing beyond the World-Honored One Mahāsaṃghādhipati, there is another Buddha named Ghoṣeśvara; that Buddha Ghoṣeśvara’s lifespan is a full one hundred million years.
Beyond the World-Honored One Sound Sovereignty, there was another Buddha named Victorious Sound; the lifespan of that Buddha Victorious Sound was a full ten billion years.
Beyond that World-Honored One Victorious Sound, there was another Buddha named Moon Face; the lifespan of that Buddha Moon Face was one day and one night.
After the World-Honored One Candrānana, there was another Buddha named Sūryānana; the lifespan of that Buddha Sūryānana was a full eighteen hundred years.
After the World-Honored One Sūryānana, there was another Buddha named Brahmānana; the lifespan of that Buddha Brahmānana was a full twenty-three thousand years.
Beyond the World-Honored One Brahmamukha, there was another Buddha named Brahmasvabhāva; the lifespan of that Buddha Brahmasvabhāva was a full eighteen hundred years.
Śāriputra! You should single-mindedly take refuge in all such Buddhas as these. Śāriputra!
Furthermore, during another eon, two hundred Buddhas appeared in the world; I shall recite their names, and you should take refuge in them.
Namo to the Buddha Yaśas-kīrti (Renowned Name)."

Śāriputra, suppose there were worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the east, worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the south, worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the west, worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the north, and worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the four intermediate directions and above and below; and suppose all those worlds, from the water’s edge below to the Peak of Existence above, were filled with motes of dust.
"Śāriputra, what do you think? Can the number of those atoms be known?
"Thus, those Tathāgatas named Śākyamuni who currently exist in the world, I see them directly before me.

Their mothers are all named Mahāmāyā; their fathers are all named King Śuddhodana; their cities are all named Kapilavastu; and their foremost śrāvaka disciples are all named Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana, while their attendant disciples are all named Ānanda—let alone those with various different names for mother, father, city, disciple, and attendant."

Śāriputra! Regarding those various worlds, in which worlds does that person place a mote of dust, and in which worlds does he not place a mote of dust? Whether those worlds in which motes are placed or those in which they are not, they extend from the water’s edge below up to the Peak of Existence above.

Furthermore, suppose there were a second person who took those atoms; for as many atoms as there were, he would cross that same number of Buddha-lands—incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of worlds—with each such world being a single step."

Śāriputra! That person takes as many worlds as there are atoms as a single step; in this manner, after traveling for hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of asaṃkhyeya kalpas, he sets down a single atom, continuing until all the atoms are exhausted.

Śāriputra! Suppose there were as many worlds as these, whether those upon which atoms have been placed or those upon which they have not; suppose these worlds were filled with atoms, and then even more atoms were added to the worlds of the ten directions.

Śāriputra! Furthermore, beyond these worlds—whether those places where atoms are placed or where they are not—consider all those worlds from the bottom, down to the water's edge, up to the pinnacle of existence (bhavāgra), filled completely with atoms.

Furthermore, there is a third person who takes that many atoms of dust, and for every number of worlds equal to those atoms, he takes a single step. He travels for hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of asaṃkhyeya kalpas before setting down a single atom, continuing in this manner until all the atoms are exhausted.

Furthermore, there is a fourth person who takes as many worlds as there are atoms in those [previously mentioned] worlds—whether they contain atoms or not—and from the bottom, reaching down to the water's edge, up to the peak of existence (bhavāgra), fills them completely with atoms.
“Śāriputra, what do you think? Can the number of those atoms be known?

"The number of those atoms may be known; however, as for those Buddhas all named Śākyamuni, their mothers all named Mahāmāyā, their fathers all named Śuddhodana, their cities all named Kapilavastu, their foremost disciples all named Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana, and their attendant disciples all named Ānanda—the number of those Buddhas cannot be known."
Śāriputra! It is the same for the fifth person, and likewise for the sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth, and tenth persons. Śāriputra!

Furthermore, there is an eleventh person who takes one atom from among those various atoms and breaks it into as many parts as there are atoms in worlds throughout the ten directions; he likewise breaks all the remaining atoms into as many parts as there are atoms in worlds throughout the ten directions.
“Śāriputra, what do you think? Can the number of those minute particles be known?

"Furthermore, suppose there is a person who takes a single step across as many Buddha-fields as there are particles of dust. With such swift supernatural power, they travel through the worlds of the eastern direction for immeasurable and boundless kalpas, dropping a single particle of dust. When the eastern direction is thus filled with these particles—whether they land or not—from the bottom at the water’s edge up to the peak of existence (bhavāgra), it is completely filled with particles;
and likewise for the southern direction, and so on up to the ten directions, from the bottom at the water’s edge up to the peak of existence, completely filled with particles."
"Śāriputra, what do you think? Can the number of those atoms be known?
"The number of those minute particles may be known;

however, the number of present-day Śākyamuni Buddhas existing in the world who share the same name—whose mothers are all named Mahāmāyā, whose fathers are all named King Śuddhodana, whose cities are all named Kapilavastu, whose foremost disciples are all named Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana, and whose attendant disciples are all named Ānanda—is beyond calculation."

How much more so for the various different names of Buddhas, different names of mothers, different names of fathers, different names of cities, different names of disciples, and different names of attendants.
Śāriputra! Even if I were to remain in the world for as many eons as there are atoms in a great many worlds, I could not finish describing even a single instance of one named Śākyamuni;
the same applies to those named Dīpaṃkara.

“Homage to the Buddhas named Devānanda; homage to the Buddhas named Dīpaprabha; homage to the Buddhas named Sarvaviśiṣṭa; homage to the Buddhas named Mahāyaśas; homage to the Buddhas named Padmottara; homage to the Buddhas named Vipaśyin; homage to the Buddhas named Śikhin; homage to the Buddhas named Viśvabhū; homage to the Buddhas named Krakucchanda; homage to the Buddhas named Kanakamuni; homage to the Buddhas named Kāśyapa. Such are the various names of the Mothers, and even the various names of the Attendants who currently dwell in the world—all these I now fully know.

At that time, the Buddha told Śāriputra:
"If good men or good women seek anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, they should first repent of all their transgressions."

If a bhikṣu has committed one of the four grave offenses (pārājika), a bhikṣuṇī one of the eight grave offenses, a śikṣamāṇā, śrāmaṇera, or śrāmaṇerī has committed a fundamental offense of the renunciant life, or if an upāsaka has violated a grave precept of an upāsaka, or an upāsikā has violated a grave precept of an upāsikā, and they wish to repent, they should bathe and purify themselves, put on new clean robes, and abstain from pungent foods and spices.

They should prepare the interior of a quiet place by adorning the ritual site (maṇḍala) with various banners and flowers, coating and painting it with fragrant mud, hanging forty-nine banners, and decorating the Buddha’s seat where an image of the Buddha is to be installed.

He burned various kinds of incense—sandalwood, aloeswood, frankincense, tagara, and sugandha—as well as various powdered incenses and unguents; he burned such diverse and wondrous fragrances and scattered various flowers.

He gave rise to great compassion, vowing to rescue suffering sentient beings: to deliver those not yet delivered, to liberate those not yet liberated, to settle those not yet settled, and to lead those not yet in *nirvāṇa* to attain *nirvāṇa*.

Day and night he contemplated the Tathāgata’s original practices and ascetic austerities, how throughout immeasurable eons he underwent all manner of suffering and affliction without ever giving rise to weariness or aversion, for the sake of seeking unsurpassed *bodhi*. Thus, toward all sentient beings, he spontaneously gave rise to a humble mind, like that of a servant.

If a bhikṣu repents for the four grave offenses (pārājika), he should, for forty-nine days—day and night—confess his transgressions before eight pure bhikṣus. He should confess once every seven days with a sincere and earnest mind, repenting of his past deeds, single-mindedly taking refuge in the Buddhas of the ten directions, invoking their names and prostrating according to his strength and capacity. If he maintains such sincerity for the full forty-nine days, his offense will certainly be extinguished.

When this person attains purification, signs shall appear—either within their waking awareness or in dreams—where they see the Buddhas of the ten directions bestowing upon them a prediction of enlightenment (*vyākaraṇa*), or see Bodhisattvas bestowing such a prediction, and are about to proceed to the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) together as companions;
or they are touched on the crown of the head by the Buddhas, manifesting the sign of the extinction of their transgressions;
or they see themselves entering a great assembly and taking their place among the multitude.
Or they may see themselves standing in the midst of the assembly preaching the Dharma;
or they may see various masters and śramaṇas of pure conduct being led to the site of enlightenment to show them the Buddhas.
If a bhikṣu, when confessing his offenses, perceives such signs, one should know that his defilements of offense have been extinguished, except in cases of a lack of sincere intent.

If a bhikṣuṇī confesses the eight grave offenses (pārājika), she should follow the same rule as for a bhikṣu; after completing forty-nine days, she shall attain purity, except in cases of a lack of sincere intent.

If a śikṣamāṇā, śrāmaṇera, or śrāmaṇerī confesses a fundamental grave offense, they must do so before four pure bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs; following the aforementioned method for a full twenty-one days, they should be known as purified, except in cases where they lack a sincere heart.

If an upāsaka or upāsikā wishes to repent for the transgressions of the heavy precepts, they should with a sincere heart revere the Triple Gem. Upon seeing a śramaṇa, they should pay respectful homage and conceive the thought that such a person is difficult to encounter. They should invite him to a place of practice and provide various offerings. They should then invite a single bhikṣu whom they hold in deep respect and confess before him all the offenses they have committed. With a sincere heart, they should repent, single-mindedly take refuge in the Buddhas of the ten directions, and recite their names while prostrating. If they continue in this manner for seven full days, they will certainly attain purity, except in cases where they lack sincerity.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
“Having attained enlightenment and subdued Māra, He dwells with mastery beneath the Bodhi tree.
He has realized the unobstructed eye and body, Which are as equal as the realm of phenomena and space.”
Surrounded by a multitude of bodhisattva disciples as numerous as the atoms in ten billion lands,
they have attained a mind of universal tranquility and are well-established in all the practices of Samantabhadra.
The Buddha’s body is wondrously adorned with the primary and secondary marks;
He emits various kinds of immeasurable light, Universally illuminating all lands throughout the ten directions— Such is the inconceivable power of all Buddhas.
I see the Buddha-lands entirely free from defilement, Filled with immeasurable, wondrous colors and purity;
All the supreme and marvelous deeds of the Buddhas, And the great assemblies, I behold through the Buddha’s spiritual power.
In the eastern world named Ratnaketu, Far removed from all defilements and wondrously adorned,
The Buddha Ratnapradīpa-vibhu currently dwells in that world at this very time.
“In the southern land of Sphāṭikadīpa, Pure, wondrous colors are everywhere adorned;
The Tathāgata Maṇiviśuddhamegha Currently dwells in the world, preaching the sublime Dharma.”
"In the western land, stainless and pure, Named the wondrous world of Sukhāvatī,
Dwells the sovereign Buddha Amitāyus, Surrounded by his bodhisattvas and disciples."
"In the northern world named Gandhapradīpa, The land is pure and most magnificently adorned,
A realm transformed by the Buddha Vimalaprabhāketu, Where he now dwells freely at the tree of the site of enlightenment."
“Lapis lazuli radiance, most wondrous color; The land is pure and supremely adorned.
The Tathāgata Buddha Unobstructed Light-Cloud Currently dwells in the northeastern quarter.”
"In the world-system Prabhāsa-ketu, where the fulfillment of all bodhisattvas is manifest,
the Buddha Svatantra-nirghoṣa currently resides there in the southeastern direction."
"In the Buddha-field of Various Delights, adorned with mani-jewels, wondrous and stainless,
where the moon of supreme wisdom is like Mount Sumeru, he is seen manifesting in the southwest."
“Manifestly beholding the Tathāgata in the northwest, In the realm of Equal Radiance of Mount Meru,
There dwells the Great Sage, the Sovereign Buddha, Surrounded by a host of disciples and bodhisattvas.”
"In the world below is the realm Sovereign Light, A pure land named Treasury of Jewel Flames;
The Buddha Amoghadarśin dwells there now, Within that wondrous land of radiant wheels."
"In the world above, the Treasury of Radiant Flames, That world is named Pure and Stainless;
The Cloud of Light from the Merit of the Universal Eye Is seen manifest, seated beneath the Bodhi tree."

“Homage to the Buddha Universal Eye Merit Radiance Cloud of the Upper Direction. At that time, Śāriputra and the great assembly, sustained by the Buddha’s spiritual power, beheld the infinite and boundless Buddhas of the past, future, and present throughout the ten directions.
At that time, Śāriputra was among the great assembly; weeping with tears streaming down his face, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
If good sons or good daughters do not resolve to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, they shall not become Buddhas.”
"From the past until now, we have been like withered grass; though we have experienced the warmth of spring, we have had no hope for the fruit of autumn.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"We pray that you will further expound at length the names of all the Buddhas throughout the ten directions; we long to hear them.
At that time, the Buddha told Śāriputra:
"You should listen with a sincere mind and attend closely; I shall speak for you."
Upon hearing of that Buddha, one should pay homage with single-minded devotion. "Śāriputra!

To the east of this world, passing through hundreds of thousands of billions of worlds, there is a buddha-field named Ratnapradīpa. In that land dwells a Buddha named Ratnasaṃcaya, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is currently preaching the Dharma."

If there are good sons or good daughters who, upon hearing the name of that Buddha, wholeheartedly receive, uphold, and mindfully recollect it, these good sons and good daughters will ultimately attain the samādhi of the seven factors of enlightenment, achieve non-retrogression from the mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and transcend sixty kalpas of the world.”
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
“In the realm of Dīpaṃkara to the east, there is a Buddha named Ratnasaṃcaya.
If anyone hears his name, they shall transcend sixty kalpas of worldly existence.”
“Śāriputra! In the eastern direction there is a world named Ratnasaṃcaya. In that world there is a Buddha named Ratnaśrī, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is currently preaching the Dharma.”

“Namo Ratnaśikhin Buddha. If a good man or a good woman hears the name of that Buddha, receives and upholds it with a sincere heart, recollects it, reads and recites it, and joins their palms in prostration;

Furthermore, if there were a son of good family or a daughter of good family who, with precious jewels filling a trichiliocosm, were to practice such giving day after day for a full hundred years, the merit of this giving would not equal even a hundredth part, a thousandth part, or a hundred-thousandth part of the merit from the aforementioned wholehearted prostration; it would not even reach a fraction thereof by any calculation or analogy.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
“In the world-realm Ratnasaṃcaya, there is a Buddha named Ratnottama; if a person hears his name, no gift would equal even a fraction of it.”

“Śāriputra! To the east from here, passing through eight hundred worlds, there is a buddha-world named Gandhavatī. In that world there is a Buddha named Siddhalokeśvararāja Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is currently preaching the Dharma.”
If a person hears the name of that Buddha, upholds it, recites it, remembers it, and pays homage to it, they will transcend five hundred kalpas of the world.
"Namo to the Buddha Accomplished Vairocana. Śāriputra!

From this world, passing eastward through a thousand worlds, there is a world named Śubhavati. In that world there is a Buddha named Vairocana-Bimbāloka Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is currently preaching the Dharma.

If good sons or good daughters hear the name of that Buddha, uphold, read, and recite it, mindfully remember it with sincerity, and pay reverent homage, they shall be liberated from the three evil realms.

From here, to the east, passing through two thousand worlds, there is a buddha-field named Immeasurable Radiance and Virtue. In that realm dwells a Buddha named Vairocana-Radiance Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.”

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family, upon hearing the name of that Buddha, prostrates with their five limbs touching the ground, reveres him with a profound mind, upholds, recites, and reads his name, and pays him respectful homage, such a person shall transcend thirty kalpas of the world.
To the east, beyond a thousand worlds, there is a buddha-field named Ramya; that Buddha is named Akṣobhya, the Arhat, the Samyak-saṃbuddha.”

If any good man or good woman hears the name of that Buddha, upholds, recites, and reads it, and pays respectful homage and prostrations, such a person will ultimately never regress from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and no demons whatsoever shall be able to disturb them.
To the east, beyond a thousand worlds, there is a buddha-field named Immeasurable. Therein dwells a buddha named Mahāprabha, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is currently preaching the Dharma.”

If any son or daughter of good family hears the name of that Buddha Prabhāsa, upholds, recites, and reads it, and pays respectful homage, such a person shall never be separated from all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and will ultimately attain the non-retrogressive mind of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

From this world, passing sixty thousand worlds to the east, there is a land named Dīpaṃkara. There dwells a Buddha named Amitaghoṣa, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is currently preaching the Dharma.”

If any son or daughter of good family hears the name of that Buddha Immeasurable Sound and recites it three times, this person will ultimately never fall into the three evil realms and will certainly attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.
"Homage to the Tathāgata Immeasurable Sound. (Recite this three times. "Śāriputra!

Beyond that world, after passing through a thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Free from Dust. There dwells a Buddha named Amitāghoṣa Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is currently preaching the Dharma."

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family, upon hearing the name of that Buddha, reveres it with a profound mind, upholds, recites, and respectfully prostrates before it, such a person shall transcend twelve kalpas of the mundane world.
Beyond twenty thousand buddha-fields, there is a world named Durjayā; there dwells a buddha named Mahāyaśas, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha.”
If a son or daughter of good family, upon hearing the name of that Buddha, joins their palms and speaks these words:

“Namo to Mahāyaśas Tathāgata,” and if there were another person who, for a full hundred years, daily gave as alms the seven treasures equal in measure to Mount Sumeru, the merit of the latter would not equal even one hundredth part of the merit of hearing this Buddha’s name and prostrating; it would not even bear comparison by calculation.
“Śāriputra! Beyond three thousand worlds, there is a land named Prabhāsa; the Buddha there is named Ratnaprabhāsa, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha.”
If good sons or good daughters accept and uphold the name of that Buddha, they shall transcend one hundred kalpas of the world and attain non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
If there are people who do not believe that hearing this name yields such merit, those people will certainly fall into the Avīci Hell for a full one hundred kalpas.

To the east, beyond ten thousand lands, there is a world named Radiant Illumination. Therein dwells a Buddha named Attainer of Great Fearlessness, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is currently preaching the Dharma.

If good sons or good daughters, upon hearing the name of that Buddha, uphold, recite, and respectfully worship it, these people will ultimately attain great fearlessness and gather an immeasurable and boundless mass of merit.
Beyond seven thousand buddha-fields, there is a world named Maṇiprabhā. There dwells a buddha named Dīpaṃkara, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently teaches the Dharma.”

If good sons or good daughters, upon hearing the name of that Buddha, reverently pay homage with a sincere heart, and uphold, maintain, read, and recite it, such persons will acquire the ten powers of the Tathāgata.
“Namo Ratnārcis Tathāgata. “Śāriputra, beyond eight thousand buddha-fields, there is a world named Satya.
In that world there is a Buddha, titled Satyaghoṣa Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells preaching the Dharma.”

If good sons or good daughters hear the name of that Buddha, uphold it, read and recite it, and pay homage with a sincere heart, such persons will ultimately attain the Four Noble Truths and ultimately attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Beyond twenty thousand buddha-fields, there is a world named Ābhā; there dwells a Buddha named Anantavimala Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is currently preaching the Dharma.”
If a son or daughter of good family hears the name of that Buddha, gives rise to sincere faith, upholds, recites, and reverently prostrates before it;

and if there were another person who offered as a gift the seven treasures filling the three-thousandfold world system, the merit of hearing the name of the Buddha Vimala and upholding and reciting it would surpass that [merit], such that the former would not equal even one part in ten million, or even beyond what can be calculated by numbers.
Why is this? If sentient beings have deep and heavy roots of sin, they shall not hear the name of the Buddha Vimala.

If there are good sons or good daughters who hear the name of this Tathāgata, these people have not planted roots of goodness under only one Buddha, nor have they planted roots of goodness under ten Buddhas; rather, these people have planted roots of goodness under hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddhas. Such people shall transcend forty-eight kalpas of the world.
“Homage to the Buddha Boundless and Stainless. “Śāriputra!
To the east, beyond nine thousand buddha-lands, there is a world named Wondrous Sound. There, a Buddha named Moon-Sound Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, currently dwells and teaches the Dharma.”

If good sons or good daughters hear the name of that Buddha, uphold, read, and recite it, and pay homage with a sincere heart, all the merit and pure dharmas they obtain will be as complete as the full moon, and they will ultimately attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Beyond ten thousand buddha-lands, there is a world named Abhaya; the Buddha there is named Anantakīrti Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells and teaches the Dharma.”
If a son or daughter of good family hears the name of that Buddha, receives and upholds it, reads and recites it, and with palms joined speaks these words:

"Namo to the Tathāgata Anantayaśas. Furthermore, if there were another person who were to give away treasures as numerous as Mount Sumeru every single day for a full hundred years, this mass of merit would not equal even one-hundredth part of the merit from upholding the Buddha’s name; indeed, it cannot be reached by calculation or analogy.

“Śāriputra! Beyond another fifteen hundred buddha-fields, there is a world named Rādhas (Lamp-Light), where a Buddha named Candrasūryaprabhāsa (Sun-Moon Radiance) Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, currently dwells and teaches the Dharma.”

If any son or daughter of good family hears the name of that Buddha, upholds, recites, and reads it, kneels with palms joined, and places their right knee on the ground, and three times utters these words:
"Namo to the World-Honored One Sun-Moon Radiance," and three times [utters this], such a person will swiftly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
“Śāriputra! Furthermore, beyond thirty thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Vimalā. There, a Buddha named Vimalaprabhā Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha currently dwells, teaching the Dharma.”

If good sons or good daughters, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, or humans and non-humans, hear these names of the Buddhas, they will ultimately never regress from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and shall not enter the evil realms.

“Śāriputra, ten thousand buddha-fields away to the east, there is a world named Śataprabhā. There, the Buddha named Viśuddhaprabha, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha, currently dwells and teaches the Dharma.”
If devas, nāgas, yakṣas, humans, or non-humans hear this name, they will certainly attain a human body and remain far removed from the afflictions of greed, hatred, and delusion.
If anyone hears this and does not believe it, they shall fall into the great hell for sixty thousand kalpas.
"Namo Qingjing Guangmingfo" (Homage to the Buddha Pure Radiance). Śāriputra!
Furthermore, beyond a hundred buddha-fields, there is a world named Śubhakṛt, where the Buddha is named Sūryaprabhā Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells there preaching the Dharma.

If a person with a thoroughly pure mind invokes the name of this Buddha, the merit they obtain will be as full as the orb of the sun; they will ultimately be able to subdue all māras and non-Buddhists, and transcend thirty kalpas of the world.

“Namo to the Buddha Sunlight! Śāriputra, furthermore, beyond sixty thousand buddha-fields, there is a world named Abiding in the Seven Factors of Enlightenment. There, the Buddha is named Anantaratna Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells and teaches the Dharma.”

If a person hears the name of that Buddha, they will fully attain the seven factors of enlightenment; they will be able to establish sentient beings within the midst of supreme jewels and ultimately achieve an immeasurable mass of merit.
Śāriputra, beyond five hundred buddha-fields, there is a world named Puṣpādarśamukha; the Buddha there is named Puṣpottama Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells there preaching the Dharma.”

If a person hears the name of that Buddha and, with faith and reverence, honors him, that person will accomplish all wholesome dharmas like the radiant blossoming of a flower and will transcend fifty-five kalpas of the world.

Beyond hundreds of thousands of billions of buddha-fields, there is a world named Sarvadaurmanasya-vigata. There, the Buddha is named Suvapuḥ-arhat-samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells and teaches the Dharma.”

If a person hears the name of that Buddha, pays homage with a sincere heart, and reads, recites, and upholds it, this person will certainly be freed from all obstacles, shall not enter the evil realms, and will transcend immeasurable kalpas of the world.

Śāriputra, beyond that, past nayuta buddha-fields, there is a world named Samatā. There dwells a Buddha named Dharmaprabhāsa-viśuddha-praphullapadma Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently teaches the Dharma.”
If any person hears the name of that Tathāgata, upholds it, and does not forget it, they shall forever be free from the three evil realms.

If bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās wish to repent of their various transgressions, they should bathe and purify themselves, don new clean robes, thoroughly cleanse the interior of the room, arrange a high seat, install an image of the Buddha, and hang twenty-five banners. With various flowers and incense, they should make offerings and recite the names of these twenty-five Buddhas, repenting during the six periods of the day and night. Upon completing twenty-five days, the four pārājika offenses, the eight prohibitions, and other such sins will be extinguished; the same applies to śikṣamāṇās, śrāmaṇeras, and śrāmaṇerīs.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
We pray only that the Tathāgata will expound the names and the lengths of the lifespans of the seven Buddhas of the past; we thirst for and delight in hearing this.”
I shall now explain this for you. Śāriputra,
ninety-one kalpas ago, there was a Buddha named Vipaśyin Tathāgata.
“Thirty kalpas ago, there was a Buddha named Śikhin Tathāgata.
Within that same kalpa, there was also a Viśvabhū Tathāgata.
From that time onward, for immeasurable and incalculable kalpas, time passed in vain without a Buddha appearing.”
In the present Bhadrakalpa, there are four Buddhas:
Krakucchanda Buddha, Kanakamuni Buddha, Kāśyapa Buddha, and I, Śākyamuni Buddha.

“Vipaśyin Buddha’s lifespan was eighty thousand kalpas; Śikhin Buddha’s lifespan was sixty thousand kalpas; Viśvabhū Buddha’s lifespan was two thousand kalpas; Krakucchanda Buddha’s lifespan was fourteen small kalpas; Kanakamuni Buddha’s lifespan was thirty small kalpas; Kāśyapa Buddha’s lifespan was twenty small kalpas; and my present lifespan is the shortest, being one hundred years.”
“Vipaśyin Buddha, Śikhin Buddha, and Viśvabhū Buddha were born into kṣatriya families.
Krakucchanda Buddha, Kanakamuni Buddha, and Kāśyapa Buddha were born into brāhmaṇa families.”
Śāriputra! I, Śākyamuni Buddha, was born into a kṣatriya family.
The three Buddhas Vipaśyin, Śikhin, and Viśvabhū were of the Kauṇḍinya clan.
Krakucchanda Buddha, Kanakamuni Buddha, and Kāśyapa Buddha—these three Buddhas were of the Kāśyapa clan.
Śāriputra! I, Śākyamuni Buddha, am of the Gautama clan.
“Vipaśyin Buddha attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi beneath a pāṭali tree.
Śikhin Buddha attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi beneath a puṇḍarīka tree.”
Vipaśyin Buddha attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi beneath a śāla tree.
Krakucchanda Buddha attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi beneath an udumbara tree.
The Buddha Kanakamuni attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi beneath a śirīṣa tree.
The Buddha Kāśyapa attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi beneath a nyagrodha tree.
Śāriputra! I, Śākyamuni Buddha, attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi beneath the aśvattha tree.
Vipaśyin Buddha convened the assembly of śrāvakas three times.
Śikhin Buddha convened the assembly of śrāvakas three times;
Viśvabhū Buddha convened the assembly of śrāvakas twice;
Krakucchanda Buddha convened the assembly of śrāvakas once.
Kanakamuni Buddha convened an assembly of śrāvakas once.
Kāśyapa Buddha convened an assembly of śrāvakas once. Śāriputra!
I, Śākyamuni Buddha, have assembled my śrāvakas once.
As for Vipaśyin Buddha, his two foremost śrāvaka disciples were named Kiṃśuka and Khaṇḍa.
The first śrāvaka disciples of Śikhin Buddha were named Jina and Vaśavartin.
The first śrāvaka disciples of Viśvabhū Buddha were named Nakṣatra and Uttara.
The first śrāvaka disciples of Krakucchanda Buddha were, first, named Ji (Swift) and second, named Li (Power).
The first śrāvaka disciples of Kanakamuni Buddha were, first, named Huodanzhi (Reviving Medicine) and second, named Pīthila.
Kāśyapa Buddha’s first two śrāvaka disciples were named Śuna and Phalada.
Śāriputra! My, Śākyamuni Buddha, first two śrāvaka disciples are named Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana.
As for the two individuals mentioned above, the former was foremost in wisdom and the latter was foremost in supernormal powers.
"The attendant of Vipaśyin Buddha was named Aśoka."
The attendant of Śikhin Buddha was named Vigatabhaya;
the attendant of Viśvabhū Buddha was named Śānta;
the attendant of Krakucchanda Buddha was named Jñāna.
The Buddha Kanakamuni had a personal attendant named Cunda;
the Buddha Kāśyapa had a personal attendant named Gavāmpati, Śāriputra!
I, Śākyamuni Buddha, have an attendant named Ānanda.
Vipaśyin Buddha had a son named Skandha.
Śikhin Buddha had a son named Aprameya.
The son of Viśvabhū Buddha was named Sudhī;
the son of Krakucchanda Buddha was named Uttara;
the son of Kanakamuni Buddha was named Jaya.
Kāśyapa Buddha’s son was named Śāstṛ. Śāriputra!
My, Śākyamuni Buddha, son is named Rāhula.
“Vipaśyin Buddha’s father was named Bandhumat, his mother was named Bandhumatī, and his city was named Bandhumatī.
Śikhin Buddha’s father was named Kona, his mother was named Vijayā, and his city was named Aruṇavatī.”
The father of Viśvabhū Buddha was named Aruṇa-devaputra; his mother was named Yaśodharā; and his city was named Manojñā.
The father of Krakucchanda Buddha was of the Brahmin caste, named Guṇa; his mother was named Vipulā; that devaputra was named Abhaya; and the city was also named Abhaya.
The Buddha Kanakamuni was of the Brahmin caste; his father’s name was Agnidatta, his mother’s name was Duryodhana, the son of a deva was named Śobha, and the city was also named Śobhā.

The Buddha Kāśyapa was of the Brahmin caste; his father’s name was Viśuddha, his mother’s name was Sujātā, and the son of heaven was named Jñānadarśin. The city was also named Jñānadarśin, which is the present-day city of Vārāṇasī.
My father’s name is now King Śuddhodana, my mother’s name is Mahāmāyā, and the city is named Kapilavastu. Śāriputra!"
One should pay homage to my original teacher, namely, Śākyamuni Buddha:

“Namo to the Buddha of Wondrous Renown; Namo to the Buddha who Subdues All; Namo to the Buddha of Kindled Lamp Light; Namo to the Fearless Buddha; Namo to the Buddha Supreme in Dharma. In this manner, during the first great asaṃkhyeya kalpa, there were eighty billion buddhas, the last of whom was named Śākyamuni Buddha.

namo to these and other Buddhas of such names, as many as they are unspeakably unspeakable.

“Homage to the Buddha Difficult to Conquer in the world-system Mālavatī, together with the Bodhisattva Banner of Light and the Bodhisattva Supreme Light as their leaders, and the assembly of immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable bodhisattvas.”

"Good sons and good daughters, those who wish to extinguish all transgressions should bathe themselves clean, put on new and pure garments, and invoke the names of these Buddhas while prostrating. They should speak thus:

'From beginningless worlds until now, I have committed unwholesome deeds through the actions of body, speech, and mind, even including slandering the Vaipulya sutras and the five heinous crimes; may they all be extinguished.'"

"Śāriputra! A son of good family or a daughter of good family who wishes to fulfill the practice of the *pāramitās*, who wishes to dedicate [their merit] toward unexcelled bodhi, and who wishes to fulfill all the *pāramitās* of the bodhisattvas, should speak these words:
'I shall learn from the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past, future, and present, and practice great relinquishment (*mahātyāga*).'"
They tore open their chests and extracted their hearts to give to sentient beings, such as the Bodhisattva Jñānavijaya and King Kāśī.
They renounced their wives, children, and so forth, bestowing them upon the poor and destitute, such as the Bodhisattva Anivartita, King Aśīlananda, Sudāna, and King Alaṃkāra.
They enter the hells to rescue suffering sentient beings, such as the Bodhisattva Mahākāruṇika and the Devaputra Sunetra;
they rescue sentient beings who engage in evil conduct, such as the Bodhisattva Sucarita and King Vijayacaryā.
He gave away his jeweled celestial crown upon his head, even peeling off his scalp to bestow it, like the Bodhisattva Uttaptavīrya and the Devaputra Ratnaśikhin;
he gave his eyes as alms, like the Bodhisattva Priyadarśana and King Candraprabha.
They gave up their ears and noses, like the Bodhisattva Aśoka and the Devaputra Vijayagāmin;
they gave away their teeth as alms, like the Bodhisattva Puṣpadanta and the Six-Tusked Elephant King.
They gave away their tongues as alms, like the Bodhisattva Avinivartanīya and King Sumukha;
they gave away their hands as alms, like the Bodhisattva Nityodyukta and King Dṛḍhamati.
They gave away their blood without regret, such as the Bodhisattva Dharmakāra and the Devaputra Candraprabha;
they gave away their flesh and marrow, such as the Bodhisattva Kṣemadatta and King Sarvamdada.
They gave away their large and small intestines, liver, lungs, spleen, and kidneys, such as the Bodhisattva Śubhavyūha and King Svayamyāpita-vipramukta-sarvapāpa;
they gave away all their limbs, both major and minor, such as the Bodhisattva Dharmeśvara and the Devaputra Jyotiṣprabha.
They sacrificed their skin and flesh, such as the Bodhisattva Viśuddhagarbha, the Golden Devaputra, and the Golden Deer King;
they sacrificed their hands and fingers, such as the Bodhisattva Dṛḍhavīrya and King Kanakavarṇa.
There are those such as the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati and the Devaputra Dharmakāma who relinquish their hands, feet, and nails;
and there are those such as the Bodhisattva Vīrya and the King Vīrya-dharmakāma who enter great pits of fire for the sake of seeking the Dharma.
For the sake of seeking the Dharma, they sold their bodies, cut open their hearts, and broke their bones to extract the marrow, as did the Bodhisattva Sadāprarudita, King Kanakavarṇa, and others.
They underwent all manner of suffering and affliction, as did the Bodhisattva Dharmapriya and the Great King Kṣipragāmin.
They relinquish the great earth of the four continents along with all its adornments, like the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta and the Devaputra Śreṣṭhaguṇacandra;
they relinquish their bodies, like the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva and King Mahābala.
I renounce my body to serve as an attendant and servant to all sentient beings suffering from poverty and affliction, just like King Śibi and others.
To state the essentials: I shall likewise accomplish all the practices, perfections, and vows of the Bodhisattvas of the past, future, and present.
I rejoice in and offer all the exquisite incense, flower garlands, and sublime music throughout the worlds of the ten directions to the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha.

Furthermore, I dedicate this merit to all sentient beings, vowing that by virtue of this merit, may all beings not fall into the evil realms; may they fulfill the eighty-four thousand practices of the *pāramitās* through this merit; may they swiftly receive the prophecy of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; may they swiftly attain the stage of non-retrogression; and may they swiftly realize unsurpassed enlightenment.

If there are sentient beings who believe my words and receive, uphold, read, and recite the names of these Buddhas, they should bathe themselves clean, put on fresh and pure garments, and at the first, middle, and last watches of the day, as well as during the three periods of the night, rise from their seats, bare their right shoulders, place their right knees upon the ground, and with a single mind invoke the names of these Buddhas, making offerings and prostrating, saying these words:
"I now pay respectful homage to all the Buddhas of the ten directions, as known by the Tathāgatas."
“Śāriputra! These sentient beings who thus make offerings and pay homage obtain immeasurable merit.

Whether they wish to attain the stage of a śrāvaka, the stage of a pratyekabuddha, or unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), they shall attain all of these by paying homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions.”

“Homage to the Buddha Emitting Radiance. This is the tenth fascicle of the *Buddhāvatamsaka-sūtra* (The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Names of Buddhas). From the first Buddha, Not-Reduced Adornment (*Anūnatālaṃkāra*), to the fifty-fifth Buddha, Dharma King (*Dharmarāja*), at the end of the fifth line of the seventh sheet, there are two hundred and ten Buddhas in total. These were already recorded in seven additional pages of the Song edition of this sutra, following the thirty-second sheet at the end of the preceding ninth fascicle.

Regarding this current duplicate section, according to the Xiang and Dan editions, it exists here but not there; thus, the preceding ninth fascicle was an erroneous duplication. Therefore, I have now removed that erroneous duplicate.

Regarding those names of Buddhas that contain characters of doubtful meaning which can be verified, I have frequently adopted them and provided annotations, noting that "other versions" refers to these readings.
*The Scripture of the Names of Buddhas Spoken by the Buddha*, Volume Eleven.

If good sons or good daughters uphold the names of these Buddhas, they will ultimately never enter hell and will swiftly attain samādhi.”
“Śāriputra! After an immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable number of kalpas beyond these buddha-names, there will be a buddha named Manuṣeśvaraghoṣa; you should take refuge in him.”

That Buddha, Svayambhūghoṣa, shall remain in the world for a lifespan of seventy million koṭis of kalpas. At his first assembly, three hundred million śrāvakas will gather, and eighty nayutas of koṭis of bodhisattvas will assemble; all of them will have attained the various supernormal powers, be endowed with the four analytical knowledges, and have reached the further shore by penetrating all emptiness.

"Śāriputra, even if I were to remain in the world for immeasurable kalpas and speak of the adornments of that Buddha’s great assembly and his land, it would be like a single drop of water from the great ocean."

Homage to the Bodhisattva Who Transcends All Paths! The Buddha said to Śāriputra:

“If there are good men or good women—whether bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās—who are able to receive, uphold, read, and recite the names of these Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, they shall never fall into the evil realms;

they will be born among gods and humans, always encounter Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), remain far removed from all afflictions (kleśa), and eventually attain great enlightenment (mahābodhi).”

When the Buddha had finished preaching this Sūtra of the Names of Buddhas, the Venerable Śāriputra, the Bhikṣu Mahānāman, and all the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās; as well as the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans and non-humans, and all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, were all greatly rejoiced. They received it upon their heads in reverence and practiced accordingly.
